steps.body:
Two different questions, and they have different answers:

**Displacement** = s(b) − s(a). Where you ended up, relative to where you began.
**Total distance** = every mile you actually covered, forwards and backwards.

If the particle never reverses, they agree. The moment it turns round, they part company — and the turning points are exactly where v changes sign.

explanationVariants: The particle turns at t = 1 and t = 3 (where v changes sign), so [0, 4] splits into three legs: [0,1], [1,3], [3,4].
You cannot compute total distance without first finding where it reversed — the legs must be measured separately and then added as positive amounts.

widget.prompt: s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t on [0, 4], with v = 3(t − 1)(t − 3). Into how many LEGS must the journey be split?

commonErrors.feedback: The particle reverses TWICE (at t = 1 and t = 3), which cuts [0, 4] into three legs: [0,1], [1,3] and [3,4].
Only if it never turned round. But v changes sign at t = 1 and again at t = 3.
Two turning points make three legs, not four.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Turns at t = 1 and t = 3 → three legs.

explanationVariants: s(4) = 64 − 96 + 36 = 4 and s(0) = 0, so the displacement is 4 − 0 = 4.
Displacement never cares what happened in between — only the two ends.

widget.prompt: s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t. Find the DISPLACEMENT over [0, 4].

commonErrors.feedback: That is the TOTAL DISTANCE, which counts every leg. Displacement is just s(4) − s(0) = 4 − 0 = 4.
s(4) = 64 − 96 + 36 = 4, not 0. (s(3) = 0, but that is a different time.)
That is only the t³ term. Compute the whole thing: 64 − 96 + 36 = 4.

widget.prompt: Walk the journey leg by leg.

panels.title: Leg one: 0 to 1
panels.body: The particle moves forward from s = 0 to s = 4. Distance covered: 4. Position now 4.

panels.title: Leg two: 1 to 3
panels.body: It reverses and slides back from 4 to s(3) = 0. Distance covered: another 4 — and distance is always counted POSITIVE, however you were facing.

panels.title: Leg three: 3 to 4
panels.body: Forward again, from 0 to s(4) = 4. Distance: 4 more. TOTAL travelled: 12. But it ends at 4, so the displacement is only 4. It covered twelve units to end up four from home.

widget.continueFeedback: Keep going — the second leg is where they part company.
widget.successFeedback: Twelve units travelled, four units displaced. The backtracking is invisible to the displacement and fully counted by the distance.

steps.body:
So the recipe for total distance is:

**Find where v = 0 and changes sign.** Those are the turns.
**Compute |s| change on each leg.**
**Add them all as positive numbers.**

In integral language — which is the next course — displacement is ∫v dt and total distance is ∫|v| dt. The absolute value is doing exactly the work you just did by hand.

explanationVariants: Every leg contributes its length as a POSITIVE number, which is exactly what taking |v| would do.

widget.prompt: The three legs run 0 → 4, then 4 → 0, then 0 → 4. Find the TOTAL DISTANCE travelled.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the DISPLACEMENT — where it ended up. The distance counts all three legs: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
That is only two legs. There are three: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
The legs cancel only if you add them with SIGNS, which is what displacement does. Distance adds their magnitudes: 12.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 units travelled, though the displacement is only 4.

hints: The particle turns only at t = 1 (where v changes sign), so [0, 2] has two legs.
explanationVariants: Total distance = 4 + 2 = 6, while the displacement is s(2) − s(0) = 2. The difference, 4, is exactly twice the backtracking.
The two numbers answer different questions, and a problem will always tell you which it wants — read carefully.

widget.prompt: s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t on [0, 2]. Find the TOTAL DISTANCE travelled.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the DISPLACEMENT, s(2) − s(0) = 2. The distance counts the backtracking: 4 forward then 2 back, so 6.
That is only the first leg (0 to 1). After the turn it slides back 2 more units, making 6 in total.
Check s(2) = 8 − 24 + 18 = 2. So the second leg is from 4 back to 2 — a distance of 2, not 6.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Legs: 0→4 (distance 4) and 4→2 (distance 2). Total = 6, though the displacement is only 2.

takeaways: Displacement is s(b) − s(a). Total distance adds the length of every leg as a positive number.
Split the journey wherever v changes sign — those are the turns, and only there.
In the next course: displacement is ∫v dt, and total distance is ∫|v| dt. The absolute value does this by hand-work automatically.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: when two quantities are linked, their RATES are linked too.

concept.body: Find where the particle turns round (v changes sign). Measure each leg separately. Add the lengths as POSITIVE numbers for distance; subtract the ends for displacement.

explanationVariants: Displacement is just the difference of the endpoints: 10 − 3 = 7.
It does not matter what happened in between.

widget.prompt: A particle starts at s = 3 and ends at s = 10, wandering back and forth in between. Find the DISPLACEMENT.

commonErrors.feedback: That is 3 + 10. Displacement is the DIFFERENCE of the endpoints: 10 − 3 = 7.
That is the final position. The displacement measures the CHANGE: 10 − 3 = 7.
